failures.triage_note: Root-caused in source: blocks/listing-detail/render.php:668 and :1026 gate the Claim trigger button behind `is_user_logged_in()` in addition to `$show_claim && ! $is_claimed && (int) $post->post_author !== get_current_user_id()`. This directly contradicts the runbook's own C.member.claim contract ('anonymous viewer on a listing's detail page sees Claim this business CTA -> clicking prompts login') and the sidebar hook comment in templates/blocks/listing-detail/sidebar.php which only renders a Claimed badge, never an unclaimed-state CTA either. Verified live: anonymous visitor on an unclaimed listing (/listing/sakura-house/, post 22, _listora_is_claimed unset) has zero 'Claim' text/button anywhere in the DOM or rendered body text. The SAME listing viewed as a logged-in non-owner (credituser) correctly shows the Claim button, opens the modal (role=dialog, aria-modal=true, focus moves in, Escape closes cleanly) - so only the anonymous discovery path is broken, not the claim flow itself once logged in.
failures.expected: Anonymous visitor on an unclaimed listing detail page sees a 'Claim this business' (or 'Claim') CTA; clicking it prompts login (per the documented contract and the login-modal helper already in the same interactivity store).
failures.actual: No Claim CTA renders anywhere on the page for a logged-out visitor. The button is entirely absent from the DOM (not hidden - never printed), so there is no way for an anonymous visitor to discover the claim feature or be routed to login.

harness_noise.note: 106+ lines of 'PHP Deprecated: Using null as an array offset...Colors.php on line 95' at session start and repeated throughout.
harness_noise.cause: WP-CLI's own bundled php-cli-tools library hitting a PHP 8.2+ deprecation on every `wp` invocation that renders colored output. Fires on ANY wp-cli call, including plain `wp plugin list`, before any Listora-specific code runs. Same class of noise already documented as harness-side in the plugin's CLAUDE.md 'Latest smoke verdict' section from the 1.7.0 run.

harness_noise.note: WordPress database error 'Unknown column rating in field list' x3 in debug.log at 06:33:22-06:33:47.
harness_noise.cause: My own `wp eval` query selected a column named `rating` on wp_listora_reviews; the real column is `overall_rating` (confirmed via DESCRIBE). Self-inflicted typo in my own ad-hoc verification query, not a plugin defect - re-run with the correct column name returned the review row cleanly.

harness_noise.note: PHP Fatal error 'Non-static method WBListora\Core\Field::sanitize_price() cannot be called statically' at 06:43:35.
harness_noise.cause: My own exploratory `wp eval` called Field::sanitize_price() as a static method without reading the class signature first (it is an instance method on includes/core/class-field.php:479). Stack trace confirms it originates in Eval_Command->__invoke from my own eval string, not from any plugin request path. No customer-facing code path calls it statically.

harness_noise.note: PHP Deprecated 'backtick operator is deprecated' inside an eval()'d code block.
harness_noise.cause: My own `wp eval` string used a shell backtick (`wp post list ...`) inside a PHP string while probing for a Job-type listing ID; harmless self-inflicted style issue in my own throwaway command, not plugin code.

harness_noise.note: '[wb-listora] Migration 1.8.0 completed.' logged twice at 06:31:35 and 06:32:09.
harness_noise.cause: Not an error - this is the Migrator's own informational log line, and it is the EXPECTED, CORRECT output of the B_upgrade test I deliberately ran (reset wb_listora_db_version to 1.6.0 twice, once via wp-cli bootstrap and once via a real front-end page load, to prove Migrator::maybe_migrate() fires and is idempotent). Recorded here for transparency, not filed as a debug_log_issue since it signals success, not failure.

F.rtl - no RTL language pack installed on this site (only en_US + de_DE per `wp language core list --status=installed`); installing Arabic mid-walk to force is_rtl() would be a site mutation beyond this run's scope. A forced `dir=rtl` client-side does not load the real *-rtl.css twins (those gate on WP's locale-driven is_rtl(), not the DOM attribute), so it would not have proven anything. Needs a follow-up run with an RTL locale installed.
